note: An IntersectionObserver rooted on the article's own scroller lights a tick for every section in view; the rail is a full-width panel clipped to its tick column with clip-path inset(), so hover or focus simply animates the clip open, and a bracket clipped to the visible range follows along. html:
Brindle KMSRunbooks 0%·6 min read

Runbook · Security

Rotate a signing key without downtime

Tokens are signed with one key and verified against every published key. Rotation is safe as long as the new key is published before it signs, and the old one stays published until its last token expires.

Before you start

Rotation takes about 40 minutes end to end, most of it waiting on caches. You need the kms:rotate role and a quiet deploy window.

Check the current key

List the active key. It should be older than 80 days; if it is younger, someone rotated recently and you can stop here.

$ brindle keys list --active
k_2026_07  ES256  active  92 days

Freeze deploys

Post in the release channel that signing is rotating. A deploy that starts mid-rotation can pin the old key into a build for up to 24 hours.

Stage the new key

Create the key as staged: it is published to verifiers but never used to sign.

Generate

$ brindle keys create --alg ES256 --state staged
created k_2026_10 (staged)

Publish to JWKS

Verifiers refetch the key set every 15 minutes. Wait two full intervals, 30 minutes, so every verifier holds both keys before anything is signed with the new one.

Cut over

Promote the staged key. New tokens are signed with k_2026_10 at once, and tokens signed with k_2026_07 still verify because both keys are published.

$ brindle keys promote k_2026_10

Retire the old key

Keep the old key published for the longest token lifetime plus an hour: 25 hours, since refresh tokens live for 24. Then retire it. Retired keys leave the key set but stay in the audit log for 400 days.

Roll back

If token verification errors rise above 0.5%, promote k_2026_07 again. Both keys are still published, so rollback is instant and nothing needs a redeploy.

Last reviewed by the platform security team on 2 October.
